To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a simulator for cardiovascular interventions that leverages a Cosserat rod model to simulate catheter/guidewires and provides a complete simulation of an angioplasty procedure.

we have created a virtual reality simulator for training of cardiovascular interventions, that leverages an inexactensible Cosserat Rod model for virtual instrument simulation, which was optimized with respect to real instruments, and that the simulator has been validated by a group of 15 interventional radiologists.
VCSim3 provides an accurate and realistic simulation of cardiovascular interventions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a VR simulator for training and research in interventional radiology.
the development of a novel simulator that can be used to teach the core skills of interventional radiology.
developing an innovative, safe, cost-effective, and effective solution for surgical training and skills assessment in the cardiovascular field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed system is a promising tool for training of cardiovascular intervention procedures.
the developed simulator is a step forward to improve the training of catheter/guidewires navigation in cardiovascular interventions.
the simulator is a promising and valuable training tool for catheter-based interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VCSim3 can provide realistic and accurate simulation of catheter/guidewires, and it can support a complete angioplasties training procedure.
we have developed the first simulator that realistically simulates the mechanical properties of the catheter/guidewires, which is a key element for the simulation of cardiovascular interventions.
VCSim3 can provide a valuable contribution to the development of future simulators for cardiovascular interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cosserat rod model is a viable solution to simulate the behaviour of catheters and guidewire in blood vessels, while providing a high degree of accuracy and computational efficiency.
it is possible to simulate the physical behaviour of a real guidewire and a real catheter navigated through a blood vessel using a Cosserat rod model.
it is possible to simulate the mechanical properties of catheters and guidewire in a realistic and accurate way, which can be used for training in the future.
